title: Data Disclosure
description: Parent User (EE1) shares personal data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) with the Authentication Service (P1) via the registration flow. This act of sharing causes a threat because the data is exposed to an untrusted or internal system.

title: Data Exposure in Transit
description: Personal data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) is transmitted between the Parent User (EE1) and the Authentication Service (P1). Data-centric threats arise here as the data itself is the medium of communication, potentially exposing sensitive information.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The Authentication Service (P1) receives the data and processes it. If the service is not properly secured or authorized, it may process the data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Authentication Service (Process P1) shares parent account data with the MongoDB users collection (DataStore DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The MongoDB users collection (DataStore DS1) receives and stores the parent account data. The minimality principle is violated if the store is not restricted to storing strictly required personal data.

title: Unrestricted JWT Issuance
description: Process P1 (Authentication Service) issues JWT tokens without verifying the parent User's identity or authorization context before sharing the token with EE1.

title: Data Exfiltration Risk
description: Process P1 shares sensitive user data (e.g., PII) with EE1 without proper access controls or encryption, creating a risk of unauthorized data leakage.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: Destination EE1 processes or stores the received JWT and user data in a way that causes privacy threats, such as storing PII in unencrypted form or using it for non-authorized analytics.

title: JWT Issuance
description: The source element (Process P1) generates a JWT containing user type information. This act of sharing the JWT with the child element (ExternalEntity EE2) exposes the user's identity and attributes to the external system, creating a potential privacy breach.
assumptions: The JWT is not encrypted or tokenized before transmission.

title: Data in Transit
description: The data-centric threat arises at the data flow (DF5). The JWT payload, which contains sensitive user attributes (userType, child profiles), is transmitted in plaintext or unencrypted format. This allows an attacker intercepting the data in transit to link or identify the user.
assumptions: No encryption or tokenization is applied to the JWT payload during transmission.

title: Data Processing
description: The destination element (ExternalEntity EE2) receives the JWT and processes it. The external system may store, use, or display the user's identity and attributes, leading to potential unauthorized access or misuse of the user's personal information.
assumptions: The external system does not have appropriate access controls or data minimization policies in place.

title: Profile Construction via Linking
description: ExternalEntity EE1 (Parent User) shares data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) with Process P3 (Child Profile Management). The combination of these quasi-identifiers (DOB, gender, govt ID) allows the system to link and identify the specific individual, enabling the creation of a profile that can be used for targeted profiling or re-identification.
assumptions: The system requires linking to meet functional requirements (e.g., session tracking), but the data elements are not sufficiently anonymized.

title: Linking in Data In Transit
description: Data-centric threat: The meta-data describing the parties involved (EE1 and P3) is transmitted over the network. This metadata can be used to identify the specific individuals involved in the data flow, facilitating the linking of the data elements at the destination.
assumptions: Standard network transmission protocols do not inherently prevent metadata leakage.

title: Processing for Profile Creation
description: At the destination element P3, the process creates a profile by combining the shared data elements. This processing action directly enables the construction of a user profile, which is a high-risk activity for privacy implications.
assumptions: The process does not apply any additional anonymization or masking techniques.

title: Child Profile Disclosure
description: Process P3 shares child profile data (id P3) with DataStore DS2 (id DS2) for storage. This constitutes a data disclosure (D) as the process explicitly transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store, potentially violating the minimality principle if not strictly required.
assumptions: Child profile data is considered personal data under LINDDUN Pro.
uncertainty_note: Assuming child profile data is personal data; verification of classification required.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: Data-centric threat: The transfer of child profile data (id P3) across the data flow (DF7) may expose meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., P3 and DS2) or the data itself, potentially linking or identifying the data subjects.
assumptions: Data-centric threats (Dd) arise from meta-data about parties or data being used to link/identify subjects.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard data-centric threats apply to this flow.

title: Child Profile Storage/Processing
description: DataStore DS2 receives and stores the child profile data (id P3). Storage or processing of personal data by the data store can cause a data disclosure (D) if the data is not strictly required or is stored in a way that facilitates further disclosure.
assumptions: Storage of personal data by a data store is considered a data disclosure (D) under LINDDUN Pro.
uncertainty_note: Assuming storage of child profile data in DS2 is considered a data disclosure.

title: Unauthorized Video Search
description: External entity EE2 (Child User) initiates a video search request without explicit authorization or consent, potentially exposing sensitive video content.
assumptions: User has not been granted specific permissions for this data flow.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: Data-centric threat: The metadata associated with the video search request (e.g., user ID, search query) may be used to link or identify the external entity EE2, facilitating unauthorized access.
assumptions: Metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: Destination element P2 (Video Management Service) processes or stores the video search data in a way that causes a threat, potentially violating privacy policies or data retention rules.
assumptions: Recipient processes or stores data in a way that causes the threat.

title: Identified Information in Metadata
description: The video metadata and file paths stored in the source element (P2) contain identified information (e.g., user IDs, specific video identifiers, timestamps). This metadata is shared with the data store (DS3), constituting a data disclosure threat where personal or identified data is transferred across a boundary.

title: Data-Centric Threat: Meta-data Linking
description: The data flow (DF9) transmits video metadata (e.g., file paths, user identifiers) in transit. This meta-data can be used to link or identify the parties involved, constituting a data disclosure threat where the transfer of identifying information across the boundary is the primary concern.

title: Data Disclosure at Destination
description: The destination element (DS3) receives the video files and metadata. If the system processes or stores this data in a way that makes it identifiable to third parties (e.g., storing user IDs in a searchable index), it constitutes a data disclosure threat where the recipient's actions cause the threat.

title: Child Search History Disclosure
description: Process P3 shares child search and watch history with DataStore DS2. This constitutes a data disclosure (transfer of personal data) across a boundary, as the process explicitly shares data intended for storage. The minimality principle is key: only strictly required personal data should be shared.
assumptions: The process is designed to store search and watch history, implying the data is considered personal and required for the service.

title: Child Search History Storage
description: DataStore DS2 receives and stores child search and watch history. The destination element processes or stores the data in a way that causes a threat, as storing personal history data creates a potential for future disclosure or misuse.
assumptions: The store is configured to persist the history data.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Data
description: External entity (EE1) shares video data with the Video Management Service (P2) without proper authentication or authorization controls. This allows unauthorized users to access sensitive video content.
assumptions: No authentication mechanism is in place for the data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the system has any form of access control or logging for the data sharing event.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow DF11 transmits video data along with metadata identifying the uploader (EE1) and the service (P2). This metadata can be used to link or identify the parties involved, potentially enabling targeted surveillance or data profiling.
assumptions: The metadata includes identifiers that could be used for identification.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard metadata includes user identifiers.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service (P2) receives the video data and stores it in a way that causes privacy threats, such as storing it in a manner that allows for improper personal data management (e.g., retention policies, access logs, or sharing with third parties not authorized by the user).
assumptions: P2 stores the data without explicit user consent or appropriate retention policies.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if P2 has implemented appropriate data retention and access controls.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The process (P2) shares video data with an external entity (EE2). This interaction is invalid under the mapping table, as external entities do not have modeled flows between each other. The sharing of video data with an external entity without a defined process interaction creates a privacy risk related to improper personal data management.
assumptions: The video data is considered personal data.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The data flow (DF12) carries video data between the process (P2) and the external entity (EE2). The invalid interaction (ExternalEntity -> Process) implies that the data in transit is being used to link or identify the parties, which is a data-centric threat related to improper personal data management.
assumptions: The video data contains identifying or personal information.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The destination element (EE2) receives the video data. The invalid interaction implies that the external entity is processing or storing the data in a way that causes a privacy threat, as it is not a valid data flow destination.
assumptions: The external entity is processing the video data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The child browsing data (personal data) is transferred from the DataStore (DS2) to the AI Recommendation Engine (P4). This constitutes a data disclosure as the data is shared across a boundary to a third party (the AI engine).
assumptions: The data transfer is intentional and designed.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Meta-data about the parties involved (DS2 and P4) is transmitted during the data flow. This metadata can be used to link or identify the data subjects, constituting a data-centric threat.
assumptions: The data flow transmits metadata about the data subjects.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) receives the data and processes it, which may involve storing or using the data in a way that causes a threat.
assumptions: The AI engine processes the data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (Process P4) shares browsing data with Third-Party Advertisers (ExternalEntity EE3). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system transfers personal data to a known third party, potentially violating the minimality principle if not strictly required.
assumptions: The data transfer is planned and intended.

title: Data Disclosure via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF14) transmits metadata about the parties involved (e.g., P4 and EE3) to advertisers. This meta-data can be used to link or identify the data subjects, constituting a data-centric threat.
assumptions: Meta-data is transmitted during the data flow.

title: Data Processing by Third-Party Advertiser
description: The Third-Party Advertiser (ExternalEntity EE3) receives and processes the browsing data. This processing may lead to further data disclosure or unauthorized use of the data.
assumptions: The advertiser processes the data in ways that cause threats.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The process P1 shares government ID images (personal data) with the data store DS4. This constitutes a data disclosure as the transfer of personal data across a boundary (from the process to the data store).

title: Data-centric Threat
description: Data-centric threats such as meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them. The flow DF15 carries metadata about the data flow itself, which could be used to identify the parties involved.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data store DS4 receives the government ID images and processes or stores them. This action of storing personal data in a way that causes a threat constitutes a data disclosure.

title: Unauthorized Access to JWT
description: The source element (Process P1) shares a JWT (JSON Web Token) in localStorage. If the JWT is compromised or if the process is triggered to retransmit it, the act of sharing causes a privacy threat. This is a data-centric threat where the act of sharing itself is the vector for potential exposure.
assumptions: The JWT is stored in localStorage and is being shared with the Browser.

title: Data in Transit (Meta-data)
description: The data flow (DF16) carries the JWT in transit. A data-centric threat arises here if meta-data about the JWT (e.g., its size, timestamp, or content hash) is used to link or identify the parties involved in the flow, potentially enabling tracking or profiling.
assumptions: The JWT is being transmitted between the Process and the DataStore.

title: Unauthorized Processing/Storage
description: The destination element (DataStore DS5) receives the JWT. If the data is processed or stored in a way that causes a privacy threat (e.g., being used to identify the user, linked to other data, or accessed without proper authorization), this is a data-centric threat at the destination.
assumptions: The JWT is stored in DS5 and is being processed or stored.

title: Profile Linking
description: Process P3 (Child Profile Management) shares data with ExternalEntity EE1 (Parent User). The process retrieves child history and associates it with the parent's identity. This linkage, potentially using recurring identifiers or quasi-identifiers common to the child profile, allows the parent to build a profile of the child, revealing additional information about the child's privacy.
assumptions: The child profile contains sufficient identifying or quasi-identifying information to be linked to the parent's identity.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the child profile contains enough quasi-identifiers to be linked to the parent's identity; depends on the specific attributes stored in P3.

title: Linking in Transit
description: The data flow DF17 carries child profile data between P3 and EE1. The act of transmitting this data, potentially including metadata about the parties involved (e.g., 'Child Profile Management' and 'Parent User'), facilitates the linking of the child's data to the parent's identity.
assumptions: The metadata associated with the data flow (e.g., entity names) is used to identify the parties.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the metadata used to identify the parties is sufficient for linking purposes.

title: Data Processing
description: At the destination (EE1), the parent user receives and processes the child profile data. The parent may use this data to build a profile of the child, which could lead to privacy implications if the parent's processing is not adequately controlled or if the child's data is used for purposes beyond the intended review.
assumptions: The parent user processes the received data to build a profile of the child.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the parent's processing of the data leads to profile building or other privacy-relevant actions.
